blocks.text: CityBond provides top-grade Aluminium Composite Panels (ACP) with a Low-Density Polyethene (LDPE) core. This core is sandwiched between two layers of solid Aluminium, each measuring 0.5mm thick. The LDPE core we use is made from a special blend of 70% Virgin LDPE and 30% LDPE, ensuring our ACPs possess superior construction properties. LDPE, a thermoplastic material that comes from the polyolefin family, has low density (0.91-0.94 g/cm3) and crystallinity levels (50-60%). This makes it very flexible for fabrication and moulding. We use ACP sheets made from LDPE, which are lightweight and easy to install, adding minimal weight to your building's structure. CityBond's ACP sheets with LDPE cores are environmentally friendly and can be recycled, falling under recycling category 4. They have strong adhesion, last long, resist impact and provide good electrical insulation. Panels also shield against corrosion caused by acids, alcohols, bases, and esters. We are happy with our quality methods and have received the IGBC certificate. This shows that we are dedicated to environmental sustainability without compromising the quality of our ACP sheets. Select CityBond's LDPE core ACP sheets for your upcoming project and see for yourself the adaptability and superiority we provide.

Everything you need to know about CityBond soffit panels — from materials and finishes to installation, maintenance and warranty.
What are soffit panels and where are they used?

Soffit panels are architectural panels installed on the underside of structures — canopies, overhangs, eaves, balconies, podiums and interior ceiling drops. CityBond ACP soffit panels add a refined visual finish while protecting these surfaces from moisture, heat, dust and pests.
What makes CityBond soffit panels different from regular ACP sheets?

CityBond soffit panels are engineered specifically for underside applications. They feature reinforced aluminium skins, advanced protective coatings, click-fit interlocking edges and trim accessories (J-trim, H-trim, inner/outer corners) that simplify installation and deliver a seamless architectural finish.
Are CityBond soffit panels suitable for outdoor applications?

Yes. The panels are weather-resistant, UV-stable and corrosion-resistant — designed for exterior overhangs, façade extensions, entrance canopies, podiums and any outdoor underside application across every Indian climate.
Are the panels termite-proof and moisture-resistant?

Absolutely. Being aluminium-based, CityBond soffit panels are inherently termite-proof, water-resistant and immune to fungal growth — making them ideal for humid coastal regions and high-rainfall zones.
What colours and finishes are available?

The current collection includes seven premium finishes — Golden Oak (CS-101), Nagpur Teak (CS-102), Pure White (CS-103), Rosewood (CS-104), Slate Grey (CS-105), Baltic Pine (CS-106) and Royal Teak (CS-107). Custom finishes can also be developed on request for large projects.
Are CityBond soffit panels fire-retardant?
Yes. FR (Fire-Retardant) grade panels are available on request and comply with modern fire safety norms. We also offer low-smoke and low-toxicity variants for commercial and high-rise applications.
Can panels be customised for curved or complex shapes?

Yes. CityBond soffit panels can be routed, folded, bent and curved to wrap soffit corners, create box-style drops, form curved canopy undersides and integrate recessed or cove lighting — perfect for complex architectural geometries.
How are the panels installed?

Installation uses a click-fit interlocking system with supporting J-trims, H-trims and corner profiles. The lightweight construction allows for rapid, hassle-free installation, even across cantilevered or complex underside structures.
Do soffit panels require regular maintenance?

Maintenance is minimal. An occasional wipe with a soft cloth and mild detergent keeps the panels looking new. The protective coating resists fading, dust buildup and stains for years of low-effort ownership.
What panel and trim sizes are available?

Standard panel lengths are 2900 mm and 960 mm. Matching J-trims, H-trims, inner corners and outer corners are available in 2900 mm lengths across all seven colours, ensuring consistent finish detailing across every application.
What warranty do CityBond soffit panels carry?

CityBond soffit panels come with up to 15 years of product warranty against manufacturing defects, delamination and coating failure under normal usage conditions, giving architects and project owners long-term confidence.
How can I request a sample or technical datasheet?

Simply reach out via the contact form above. Our team will share the finish sample book, technical datasheets, installation guidelines and connect you with a regional fabricator partner for site support.

body.title: Start with the setting
body.text: Look at the space around your project before choosing a finish. Notice its daylight, neighbouring materials and the surfaces people will see at close range. A palette feels more coherent when these details are considered together.

body.title: Give each material a purpose
body.text: Choose one finish to lead, then use supporting tones to create balance. A warm grain, a quiet solid colour and a reflective accent can play different roles. Compare physical samples together instead of judging each one in isolation.

body.title: Take the next step
body.text: Collect photographs, drawings and the finishes you are considering. Share them with the CityBond team to discuss suitable options, sample availability and the specifications your project needs.

body.title: Look at different times
body.text: A surface can appear very different in morning light and late afternoon shadow. Observe the site from the viewpoints that matter to the project and record how its form changes through the day.

body.title: Think in layers
body.text: Panel joints, returns and the rhythm of an elevation are part of the composition. Review the overall pattern alongside close-up details so that the material choice supports the building’s proportions.

body.title: Discuss the complete system
body.text: Finish selection is one part of a facade decision. Ask the project team to review the proposed panel, fixing system and applicable project requirements together before a final specification is issued.

body.title: Make a physical comparison
body.text: Digital images are a useful starting point, but a physical sample helps you judge texture and reflectivity. Place samples beside other planned materials and look at them from more than one angle.

body.title: Record the details
body.text: Keep the sample reference, finish name and supplier information with your project notes. Ask the team to confirm the current product specification and availability before placing an order.

body.title: Share the context
body.text: A photograph of your sample arrangement can help explain the direction you want to explore. Add a note about where each material will be used so that the conversation stays connected to the design.

body.title: Describe the application
body.text: Start with the location, the type of project and the surfaces you want to work on. Explain the visual direction in a few clear sentences and include drawings or photographs where they help.

body.title: List the questions
body.text: Write down what is still to be decided: finish, dimensions, installation details or sample selection. A concise list makes it easier for the project team to identify the next steps.

body.title: Keep a shared record
body.text: Record the agreed references and decisions as the project develops. A useful brief grows with the work and helps everyone understand why a material or detail was chosen.
